# Conclusion

Trust, in the setting this paper formalizes, is not a residual category
for whatever verification happens not to reach. Above a floor of two
named physical residuals, it factors into exactly three causes —
determination, certifiability, monotonicity — each proved, not
postulated, to be exhaustive; each naming a specific anchor a verifier
must rely on; each priced by a distinct, named repair. Two axes of the
three live inside an algebra synthetic topology has studied for four
decades; the third is tested, independently, by archival science's own
empirical methods. None of the three subfields this paper draws its
axes from composes them, and none states the biconditional this paper's
Lean artifact proves.

The result is stated once, at the strata where it is proved, honestly
marked where it is not yet proved, and demonstrated on two independent
domains rather than one — because a claim of generality that rests on a
single instance is a special case wearing a general theorem's clothes,
and this paper does not want to be that. What remains open — the
polynomial stratum, the source-integrity instantiation's frontier
tightness results, the entailment calculus this paper deliberately keeps
parked — is stated as open, not smoothed over, in keeping with the
posture the whole paper tries to hold: minimize trust is not a slogan
here. It is a theorem's exact accounting of where verification ends and
who is asked to stand in for it.
